display.purpose: Antonio 700 uppercase, min(25vw, 40svh) on mobile and clamp(3rem, 18vw, 16rem) from 768px, 0.05em tracking. The name only; the source shape the dot field samples.

statement.purpose: Antonio 700 uppercase, line-height 0.95, Lamp White. The one big line per screen, sized from its column as min(cap, k·cqi + rem, h·svh): 176px default (a project title, I am Criztian., Let's connect.), 127px for Development, 136px belief, 120px client, 128px contact at 1440. FAQ has none since Phase 12: its numbered questions carry the screen.

numeral.purpose: Antonio 700 digits, line-height 0.86, a 2px outline and no fill (Lit Grey active, Wire Grey neighbours). How I work step numbers only, 45svh less 9.5rem from 48rem (96px to 320px), 17.8svh on a phone (72px to 150px). Decorative and aria-hidden.

title.purpose: Antonio 700 uppercase, clamp(2.75rem, 2.47rem + 1.14vw, 3.5rem), line-height 0.95. How I work step titles and About stat values; 32px on short phones.

section-label.purpose: Antonio 700 uppercase, 18px on a phone and 20px from 768px, 0.04em tracking, in a 16px line box. The one h2 style: the name in Lamp White, the position count (· 02 / 03) in Dim Grey.

arrival-title.purpose: The section label's own name at min(8rem, 17cqi, 14svh), about 122px at 1440×900. Big while the section scrolls in, docked into the label by the time the dots land. Never a second element; FAQ has none.

body.purpose: Geist 400, 15px/1.55 on a phone and 18px/1.5 from 768px, Lit Grey, at most 40ch. Paragraphs under statements, the About story, FAQ answers.

lede.purpose: Geist 400 uppercase, 14px/1.625 with 0.14em tracking from 768px, 13px/1.7 with 0.05em on mobile. The hero tagline only, max 34rem.

label.purpose: Geist 400 uppercase, 14px, 0.025em tracking. Nav links and the Contact action; the project tag at 12px; the submit button in Geist 500.

item.purpose: Geist 400 uppercase, 13px/16px, 0.08em tracking, Lit Grey after a Dim Grey tabular number. Numbered lists such as the service items, on Rule Grey hairlines.

cue.purpose: Geist 400 uppercase, 11px, 0.22em tracking, Dim Grey. The scroll cue, plate chips, captions, the email line and the footer bar.

question.purpose: Antonio 700 uppercase, 26px on desktop and 20px on a phone, line-height 1.05, 0.02em tracking, Lit Grey (Lamp White while open), after a Dim Grey Antonio number. The FAQ questions only (Phase 12).

field-label.purpose: Geist 500 uppercase, 12px on a 16px line that grows only when the label wraps, 0.08em tracking, Lamp White, 10px after an aria-hidden Dim Grey Antonio 700 number at 14px. The contact form's four labels and the service chips' text (Phase 12).

motion.name: ease-signal
motion.purpose: The one ease: the wordmark intro, the light sweep, the wheel turn, the nav dot, the cursor, the menu wipe.

motion.name: intro-sweep
motion.purpose: Left-to-right reveal of the ghost wordmark (14%), 26px feather; the only soft-edged sweep.

motion.name: light-sweep
motion.value: hard-edged wipe, 24px slide, driven by the dots' progress
motion.purpose: Every section's label, statement and copy sweep in as the dots land and out as they leave, one line at a time (0.15 line stagger). Never on a clock.

motion.name: pen-draw
motion.value: 1.6s per drawing, triggered 12% into a transit
motion.purpose: Step scenes (Projects, Services, How I work) trigger and play by themselves; the scroll is never held.

motion.name: copy-drift
motion.value: up to 40px, from 48rem, on the screen's view timeline
motion.purpose: Single-frame screens' copy drifts against its dot object as the screen arrives and leaves; 0 while pinned.

motion.name: arrival-title
motion.value: scroll-linked, docks on the signal ease as the dots land
motion.purpose: A section's label arrives big and shrinks into the label as the section pins.

motion.name: header-solid
motion.purpose: Header turns black at 80% with a backdrop blur and a Rule Grey bottom rule past 120px of scroll.

motion.name: indicator
motion.purpose: The nav dot slide and the cursor's state changes.

motion.name: menu-wipe
motion.purpose: Mobile menu panel wipes open from the top.

motion.name: faq-open
motion.purpose: FAQ answer opens and its plus turns 45°.

motion.name: lift
motion.purpose: Tagline and scroll cue rise in after the intro settles.

breakpoints.name: short
breakpoints.value: short screens; tightens frame insets, step type and copy budget

components.css: .ds-contact-stage { background: #000000; padding: 24px; } .ds-contact { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; font-family: Geist, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; letter-spacing: 0.025em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #000000; background: #ffffff; text-decoration: none; padding: 10px 20px; border-radius: 0; transition: background-color 0.15s; } .ds-contact:hover { background: #cccccc; } .ds-contact:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.5); }

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Form submit: square Lamp White fill, Unlit Black text, 48px tall, Geist 500 in the uppercase Label voice. Hover dims to 80%, active nudges down 1px.
components.css: .ds-btn-stage { background: #000000; padding: 24px; } .ds-btn-primary { font-family: Geist, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.025em; text-transform: uppercase; height: 48px; padding: 0 20px; background: #ffffff; color: #000000; border: 0; border-radius: 0; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s, transform 0.1s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.8); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.5); }

components.name: Adaptive Cursor
components.description: Desktop mouse only: a 6px white dot at the pointer and a 36px 1px hairline ring at 40% trailing it, both mix-blend-mode difference. Over an action the ring fills to a 56px disc with the dot as a hole.
components.css: .ds-cursor-stage { position: relative; background: #000000; height: 120px; } .ds-cursor-ring, .ds-cursor-dot { position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 50%; border-radius: 50%; mix-blend-mode: difference; pointer-events: none; } .ds-cursor-ring { width: 36px; height: 36px; margin: -18px 0 0 -18px; border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.4); } .ds-cursor-dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; margin: -3px 0 0 -3px; background: #ffffff; }

components.name: Scroll Cue
components.description: Cue type in Dim Grey with a 14px down-right arrow, pinned 40px from the bottom of the hero stage.
components.html: Scroll to explore
components.css: .ds-cue-stage { background: #000000; padding: 24px; display: flex; justify-content: center; } .ds-cue { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; font-family: Geist, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; line-height: 1.5; letter-spacing: 0.22em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #999999; text-decoration: none; transition: color 0.15s; } .ds-cue:hover { color: #ffffff; } .ds-cue:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.5); outline-offset: 4px; }

narrative.overview:
The site is a dark room with a display board. The name Criztian is not typeset. It is built from thousands of points of light that sit on black, scatter from a cursor or a finger, and spring back with a bounce.

The one idea: the dots build one product. As the visitor scrolls, the name's dots become the idea (a turning cube) and frame the finished work. Then they build one product stage by stage: the mark, the mark in a page layout, and the layout opening into code; then the same page listened for, planned, wireframed, built and launched. They frame the real people behind the work, draw the conversation beside the questions, shake hands, gather round the contact form, and end on an invitation in the name's own lettering: LET'S BUILD. A client should leave remembering one sentence: "I build whole products."

The page rule: every screen shows one dot object and one big, bold statement. Everything else is quiet signage. On FAQ the numbered questions carry the screen in place of a statement.

The world is black throughout and strictly monochrome. Hierarchy is set by how brightly something is lit (full white, three-quarter, dimmed, ghost), never by hue. Every corner is square, because signage and hardware are square. The feeling is calm, precise and premium.

This file describes the public site. The owner surfaces (/login, /dashboard, the editor and the contact inbox) are tools that use the stock shadcn neutral system with light and dark modes. Only the Square Signal Rule reaches them, because it is set at the token level. The inbox (Phase 13, the owner's pick of the stock look) is a list beside the open message on desktop and one screen each on a phone; a new message is marked by a small round dot and a bold name, the one curve on the owner side.
keyCharacteristics: Black ground from hero to footer, with no texture. The public page ignores the OS colour scheme.
One dot object and one statement per screen (FAQ's numbered questions stand in for its statement).
One display voice (Antonio, uppercase) and one working voice (Geist).
Brightness is the only emphasis tool. No accent hue.
Zero radius. Dots are the only curves; the How I work ring is drawn in dots, and the cursor's ring is the one hairline circle.
The dots are decorative. A real <h1> always carries the name, and real text carries every statement.

rules.name: The Light-Is-Emphasis Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from brightness alone: lamp white, then lit, dim and ghost. If something needs more attention, light it brighter. Never give it a colour.

rules.name: The Ghost Rule
rules.body: Ghost Grey never carries text a visitor has to read. If it must be read, it is Dim Grey or brighter.

rules.name: The Always-Night Rule
rules.body: The public page is black from top to bottom in every OS colour scheme. The owner can retune the theme colours in the editor, but the seeded defaults stay dark.

rules.name: The One-Statement Rule
rules.body: Big type is emphasis only: the name, the belief line, one statement per section and the How I work numerals. A screen never has two statements, and a pinned section's name is never big type: it is the section label. The one exception is the arrival title, which is big only while its section scrolls in and is docked by the time the dots land.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Antonio is for the name, statements, titles, section labels and numerals. Geist handles everything else. There is no third voice, and there is no mixed-case Antonio.

rules.name: The Tracked Signage Rule
rules.body: Uppercase Geist is always tracked out. Uppercase text at default tracking reads as shouting, not signage.

rules.name: The Split Rule
rules.body: The statement is on the left and the object on the right; on a phone the object comes first. The composition axis never changes from one section to the next, with one exception: the Wheel.

rules.name: The Wheel Rule
rules.body: How I work turns on a wheel, and a wheel only reads as a real rotation when its centre is the screen's centre. So How I work stacks on the centre axis at every width: the shape above, the numeral on the top of the ring, the title and copy under it, the neighbouring steps dim at both edges. Its label stays top left.

rules.name: The Stage Rule
rules.body: The hero owns the first viewport. Nothing else competes above the fold, not even a secondary call to action.

rules.name: The Lit-Not-Lifted Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the public site gets a box-shadow or a raised surface. When something needs to come forward, it gets brighter. A plate is framed by dots, never by a border or a shadow.

rules.name: The Square Signal Rule
rules.body: Zero radius everywhere. The only round things on the site are dots, rings drawn in dots, and the cursor's 1px hairline ring.

rules.name: The One-Motion Rule
rules.body: Section content moves in one of four ways, and no section gets its own trick: the light sweep (a hard-edged left-to-right wipe with a 24px slide, drawn by the dots' progress, never a clock); the pen-order draw of the dots; the desktop copy drift (up to 40px, still while pinned); and the arrival title, which docks into the label as the dots land.

rules.name: The One-Scroll Rule
rules.body: Trigger, play, no lock. Inside a scene with steps, a step triggers once the scroll passes 12% into a transit, in either direction, and then plays by itself (1.6s for a drawing). The page never holds the scroll; a fast scroll carries on and the next trigger takes over. Between scenes the flight follows the scroll.

rules.name: The Breather
rules.body: Every section after the hero starts three-quarters of a screen of black below the one before (owner, Phase 12). The old section's copy sweeps out as it rises, the dots fly across the black, and only then does the next section's title sweep in, so a transition reads as its own moment and even a fast scroll never stacks two sections' text. The old section's bottom edge is still on screen as the next one's top comes up, so the screen is never empty. FAQ's drawing holds only a quarter of a screen after its questions and Let's connect adds only a quarter of a screen, so the conversation never sits alone on black. It is space, not a pin; it goes where the dots can't run (no WebGL2, no JavaScript) and stays under reduced motion and the pause, so a motion setting never changes the page's length.

rules.name: The Moving-Line Rule
rules.body: A drawn line that travels (the ring's dots, the numerals' outlines, a drawing hairline) is never Lamp White; it is Lit Grey or Wire Grey. Lamp White is for settled, lit states. The dot field is exempt.

rules.name: The Draw-and-Frame Rule
rules.body: The dots draw ideas and frame real things. Ideas are drawn in dots: the name, the cube, the product being built. Real things (a project image, the owner's photo, a client's plate, the form) are framed by dots, never made of them. A dot object is never shrunk into a corner, and no screen has a background texture.

rules.name: Reduced Motion
rules.body: No sweep, draw, flight, spin, wobble, drift, arrival title or count. Text appears in place, each shape is drawn still in its resting pose only while its section is pinned, and the canvas is empty between scenes. The scroll-progress hairline stays, because it moves only with the reader's own scroll.

rules.name: Pause Motion
rules.body: The header's square toggle gives the reduced-motion page to anyone (WCAG 2.2.2). Paused, the cube and the Services stages stop turning and the browser remembers the choice. Where the system already asks for reduced motion the toggle is hidden.

dos: Do give every screen one dot object and one statement (FAQ's numbered questions stand in for its statement), and keep everything else quiet signage.
Do open every section from Projects to Contact with the section label <h2>: bold Antonio, the name in Lamp White, the count in Dim Grey.
Do keep every public section on plain Unlit Black (#000000) and express hierarchy through brightness steps: Lamp White, Lit Grey, Dim Grey.
Do set the name, statements, titles, section labels and numerals in Antonio 700 uppercase and everything else in Geist.
Do track out uppercase Geist (0.025em for labels, 0.08em for items, 0.14em for the lede, 0.22em for cues).
Do draw ideas in dots and frame real things with dots.
Do let the scroll trigger a step and let it play by itself.
Do keep a real, readable <h1> behind the dot field, and mark only decorative leaves aria-hidden.
Do route every motion through the reduced-motion preference and the pause toggle.
Do square corners through the --radius token rather than by editing vendored components.
donts: Don't introduce an accent hue, gradient, tinted surface or background texture. The palette is white at different intensities on black.
Don't use a border radius anywhere. The only round things are dots, rings drawn in dots, and the cursor's ring.
Don't use shadows or raised cards. Brightness, not elevation, brings things forward.
Don't put readable text in Ghost Grey (#737373). It fails AA at body sizes.
Don't outline anything interactive in Rule Grey (#1f1f1f). It is for dividers.
Don't fill a surface with Lamp White unless it is an action (the Contact action, the submit button).
Don't put two statements on one screen, or set a section's name in big type once it has pinned.
Don't render a real thing (a photo, a project image, a logo) in dots, or shrink a dot object into a corner.
Don't hold the scroll, or give a section a content effect outside the light sweep, the pen draw, the desktop copy drift and the arrival title.
Don't let the public page follow the OS light or dark scheme.
Don't lift copy, layouts or components from the reference sites, or design a section against one.
